sections.h2: How is Nebraska organized when you sell a house here?
sections.html:
Nebraska has 93 counties, and almost every step of a home sale runs through the one where the house sits. The county assessor values the property, the county treasurer collects the tax, and the register of deeds records the deed. There is no statewide deed registry, so a house in Omaha and a farmhouse in the Panhandle are handled by different offices.

The ten cities we cover most often sit in nine counties. Omaha is in Douglas County, Lincoln in Lancaster, Bellevue and Papillion in Sarpy, Grand Island in Hall, Kearney in Buffalo, Fremont in Dodge, Norfolk in Madison, Columbus in Platte and Hastings in Adams. Find your county in the list further down this page and open its guide for office details.

  • County assessor: value and valuation notice
  • County treasurer: tax statements, payoff figures, delinquent tax
  • Register of deeds: recording the deed and the transfer statement
  • County court: probate and inheritance tax for an estate

sections.h2: When are Nebraska property taxes due, and what happens if they go unpaid?
sections.html:
Half of the tax becomes delinquent on May 1 and the other half on September 1, with one change: counties over 100,000 people use April 1 and August 1. That rule is in Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-204. Ask your county treasurer which date applies to you.

An unpaid tax bill stays attached to the house. At closing, the title company normally pulls a payoff from the treasurer and settles any unpaid amount from the proceeds. If you are behind, ask the treasurer for a current figure before you list or accept an offer. Our Nebraska property tax guide walks through appeals and selling with tax due, and the homestead exemption page covers the state program for qualifying owners.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a deed in Nebraska?
sections.html:
The state charges a documentary stamp tax on the grantor, set at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, for transfers before January 1, 2032. For transfers on or after that date the written rate drops to $2.32. The statute measures value by the full consideration paid, including any liens the buyer assumes. On a $200,000 sale the tax works out to $664.

Several deeds are exempt. Section 76-902 lists, among others, deeds between spouses or between parent and child without payment, deeds of distribution from a personal representative to heirs, transfer on death deeds, and deeds that secure or release a debt. The register of deeds presumes a deed taxable unless the face of the deed or your paperwork shows an exemption, so name the exemption when you file.

Recording itself is a county matter. Our guides to recording a deed, the quitclaim deed and the transfer on death deed explain forms and fees. Ask the register of deeds in your county for the current fee schedule and accepted payment types.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in Nebraska?
sections.html:
Most Nebraska home loans are secured by a trust deed, and a trust deed can be foreclosed by a trustee sale without a lawsuit. The Nebraska Trust Deeds Act sets the steps, and they are short enough that an owner who waits can run out of room quickly.

  • The trustee or its attorney records a notice of default with the register of deeds in each county where the property sits.
  • At least one month must pass before notice of sale goes out. The wait is two months for farm property that is outside a city or village and meets the statute's conditions.
  • The notice of sale runs in a county newspaper once a week for five weeks, and the last publication must fall between ten and thirty days before the sale.
  • The sale takes place between nine in the morning and five in the afternoon at the premises, the courthouse or another county public building.

During the cure window, the owner or a junior lienholder can pay everything due plus enforcement costs and capped trustee fees, and the loan is reinstated (section 76-1012). Selling the house before the auction is another way out, and a cash purchase can close in days when the payoff is clear. Our Nebraska guides by city and county list the local pages. Check your loan papers or ask an attorney which security document you signed.

sections.h2: What happens to a Nebraska house after the owner dies?
sections.html:
Probate is a county court matter, and no one can sign a deed for the estate until a personal representative is appointed or another lawful transfer route is in place. Once the court appoints a representative, the clerk publishes a notice to creditors once a week for three weeks. Creditors then have two months from the first publication to present claims, and the first publication must happen within thirty days of the appointment (section 30-2483). If the person who died was 55 or older, or lived in a medical institution, the notice must also go to the Department of Health and Human Services.

Nebraska charges an inheritance tax, paid by the heir who receives the property. For deaths on or after January 1, 2023, close relatives such as children, parents and siblings pay 1 percent on the value they receive above $100,000. A surviving spouse owes nothing on what passes to them, and so does an heir under 22 who falls in the close-relative class (section 77-2004). Other relationships pay higher rates on smaller exempt amounts, and the county court makes the final call.

Deeds of distribution from a personal representative to heirs carry no stamp tax. For the full walkthrough, read our probate guide and the inheritance tax guide, and ask the county court clerk where the estate is filed about current forms.

sections.h2: What should a landlord know before selling a house with tenants?
sections.html:
Residential leases fall under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act in Chapter 76 of the Nebraska statutes. The notice periods are short, and a court order is still needed to remove a tenant.

  • Unpaid rent: seven calendar days after written notice, and the tenant can stop the process by paying in that time (76-1431).
  • Material lease breach: written notice that ends the lease no sooner than thirty days after receipt unless the tenant fixes the problem within fourteen days.
  • Same breach within six months: at least fourteen days' written notice.
  • Violent crime or illegal drug sales on the premises: five days' written notice with no right to cure.

Security deposits matter at closing. A landlord may not take more than one month's rent as a deposit, apart from a pet deposit of up to one quarter of a month's rent, and the balance with an itemization is due within fourteen days after the tenancy ends. The statute binds whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends, which is why sellers and buyers should agree in writing on the deposit amount. See our landlord and tenant guide and eviction notice guide.

sections.h2: What does a cash as-is sale mean in Nebraska?
sections.html:
A cash as-is sale means the buyer pays without a mortgage and takes the house in its current condition, so repairs, cleanouts and lender appraisals drop out of the timeline. It does not change the legal steps for the deed. The seller still signs a deed, the buyer or the buyer's agent still files the real estate transfer statement with the register of deeds, and the stamp tax still applies unless an exemption fits.

Sellers who benefit most from this route usually share one of a few situations.

  • An inherited house that needs repairs and has several heirs
  • A rental with a tenant in place, or one with deferred repairs
  • A home with a trust deed in default and a sale date approaching
  • A property with unpaid tax and no cash to fix the roof or the furnace

Before you sign, ask who will prepare the deed and the transfer statement and what that costs. Your county register of deeds can tell you what it needs at filing.

faqs.q: How many counties does Nebraska have?
faqs.a: Nebraska has 93 counties. Each one has its own assessor, treasurer and register of deeds, so the office you call depends on where the house is.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Nebraska if I owe back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the county treasurer for a current payoff figure first, because delinquent tax accrues and the due dates differ in counties over 100,000 people.

faqs.q: How long does a Nebraska trust deed foreclosure take?
faqs.a: The statute requires at least one month between the notice of default and the notice of sale, then five weekly newspaper publications before the auction. The owner can reinstate the loan within the cure window by paying what is due.

faqs.q: Does Nebraska have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The heir who receives the property pays it. For deaths on or after January 1, 2023, close relatives pay 1 percent on value above $100,000, and a surviving spouse pays nothing on what passes to them.

faqs.q: What is the Nebraska deed stamp tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for transfers before January 1, 2032. Some deeds are exempt, including parent to child deeds without payment and deeds of distribution from an estate.

faqs.q: How much notice must a landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven calendar days in writing, and the tenant can cure by paying within that period. A court order is still required to remove a tenant.

faqs.q: Who do I call to check a deed or tax record?
faqs.a: Call the register of deeds for deeds and the county treasurer for tax in the county where the house sits. Our county guides list the offices we have confirmed.
